newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices gain on active mill buying.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices gain on active mill buying.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Friday rose with spinning mills remaining active buyers after the government allowed more exports of cotton yarn, dealers said.
A shortage of ready stock on scattered arrivals also dragged prices up.

In spot deals Bengal-deshi rose by 15 rupees at 915/955 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned rose by 10/15 rupees to 1,565/1,670 rupees per maund. Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) lifted by 200 rupees at 13,500/14,000 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
"The government recently allowed export of 20 million kg of cotton yarn and traders were expecting fresh release of export quota for cotton yarn in the coming days," one broker said.
"The higher export of cotton yarn will lead to higher purchases of cotton by the spinning mills," he added.
Sentiments at the close were firm amid negligible arrivals due to an ongoing strike by the transport operators.
